android.desc:
Turn your Android phone or tablet into a Mac trackpad, keyboard and mouse. Remote Magic Trackpad connects to your Mac over Bluetooth and gives you a wireless touchpad with full macOS gestures: Mission Control, App Exposé and Spaces.

Use it at your desk as a remote trackpad for Mac, or from across the room as a Mac remote. It is an input device, not screen sharing: you keep watching your Mac's own display.

Phone as trackpad for Mac: what you need
• A Mac with Apple silicon (M1 or later) on macOS 13 or later; Intel Macs won't work
• The free macOS companion app from themythicalengineer.com/apps/remote-magic-trackpad/
• A phone or tablet on Android 7.0 or later

How to connect
1. Install and open the companion app on your Mac. It runs in the menu bar.
2. If macOS blocks it, click Open Anyway in System Settings > Privacy & Security.
3. Allow Bluetooth, Accessibility and Input Monitoring.
4. Open this app on your phone, allow Nearby devices and keep it open. No Bluetooth pairing needed.
Stuck on Scanning for devices? Disconnect other Bluetooth devices from your Mac.

What you get
• No extra hardware: a Bluetooth trackpad that links straight to your Mac
• Phone as trackpad for Mac: switch apps, desktops and windows with a swipe
• Phone as mouse for Mac: point, click, right-click, scroll and drag
• Type with Command, Option and the shortcuts you know on a Bluetooth keyboard for Mac
• Mac remote control from your seat: volume, brightness and playback on the function row
• Point and type on one screen: Combined Mode puts the trackpad above Gboard swipe typing

Mac trackpad gestures
• One finger moves the cursor; tap to click, two-finger tap to right-click
• Two-finger scroll, vertical and horizontal
• Pinch to zoom, two-finger rotate and smart zoom with a two-finger double-tap
• Two-finger swipe left or right to go back and forward
• Three-finger drag to move windows and select text
• Four fingers: swipe up for Mission Control, down for App Exposé, left or right to switch Spaces
• Four-finger pinch for Launchpad, spread for Show Desktop

Bluetooth keyboard for Mac: all 78 keys
• Command (⌘), Option (⌥), Control (⌃), Shift and Fn for shortcuts like Cmd+C, Cmd+V and Cmd+Tab
• Function row for brightness, volume and playback, plus F1–F12 via Fn
• Key repeat for letters, arrows and delete
• Four mechanical keyboard sound profiles and haptic feedback as you type
